verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              सन्तिष्ठत प्रहरत तूर्णं विपरिधावत। इति स्म सैन्धवो राजा चोदयामास तान् नृपान्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said: In the interval, the king of Sindhu was commanding the princes saying, “Halt, strike, march quick."

verses.sanskrit: ततो घोरतमः शब्दो रणे समभवत् तदा। भीमार्जुनयमान् दृष्ट्वा सैन्यानां सयुधिष्ठिरान्॥२॥
verses.english: Then there arose a dreadful noise in the encounter when the soldiers saw, Bhima, Arjuna and the twin brothers with Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: शिबिसौवीरसिन्धूनां विषादश्चाप्यजायत। तान् दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्रान् व्याघ्रानिव बलोत्कटान्॥३॥
verses.english: Seeing those powerful heroes like dreadful tigers the heroes of Shibi, Sauvira and Sindhu tribes lost heart.

verses.sanskrit: हेमचित्रसमुत्सेधां सर्वशैक्यायसीं गदाम्। प्रगृह्याभ्यद्रवद्भीमः सैन्धवं कालचोदितम्॥४॥
verses.english: Then armed with a mace made entirely of Shaikya iron and coated with gold, Bhimasena rushed towards the Saindhava king doomed to death.

verses.sanskrit: तदन्तरमथावृत्य कोटिकास्योऽभ्यहारयत्। महता रथवंशेन परिवार्य वृकोदरम्॥५॥
verses.english: Thereupon quickly encircling Vrikodara with mighty charioteers Kotikasya interposed between and separated the combatants.

verses.sanskrit: शक्तितोमरनाराचैर्वीरबाहुप्रचोदितैः। कीर्यमाणोऽपि बहुभिर्न स्म भीमोऽभ्यकम्पत॥६॥
verses.english: And although assailed by many clubs and iron shafts hurled at him by the mighty arms of hostile heroes, Bhima did not waver for a moment.
verses.bhavadeepa: अन्तरमभ्यहारयत् भीमजयद्रथयोर्मध्ये प्रवेशेन व्यवधानं कृतवान् । रथवंशेन रथवर्गेण॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: गजं तु स गजारोहं पदातींश्च चतुर्दश। जघान गदया भीमः सैन्धवध्वजिनीमुखे॥७॥
verses.english: But he slew, with mace, an elephant with its driver and fourteen foot-soldiers fighting in front of a Jayadratha's chariot.

verses.sanskrit: पार्थः पञ्चशतान् शूरान् पार्वतीयान् महारथान्। परीप्समानः सौवीरं जघान ध्वजिनीमुखे॥८॥
verses.english: Wishing to seize the Sauvira king, Partha too killed five hundred brave mountaineers fighting in the van of the Sindhu army.

verses.sanskrit: राजा स्वयं सुवीराणां प्रवराणां प्रहारिणाम्। निमेषमात्रेण शतं जघान समरे तदा॥९॥
verses.english: In the twinkling of an eye the king himself destroyed, in that encounter, the flowers of the Sauviras.

verses.sanskrit: ददृशे नकुलस्तत्र रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य खड्गधृक्। शिरांसि पादरक्षाणां बीजवत् प्रवपन्मुहुः॥१०॥
verses.english: And Nakula was seen there coming down from the chariot, with a sword in hand and scattering in no time the heads of the battalions fighting on the rear like a cultivator sowing seeds.

verses.sanskrit: सहदेवस्तु संयाय रथेन गजयोधिनः। पातयामास नाराचैर्द्रुमेभ्य इव बर्हिणः॥११॥
verses.english: From his chariot, Sahadeva began to cut down with his iron arrows, many heroes fighting on elephants like birds dropped from the branches of a tree.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्त्रिगर्तः सधनुरवतीर्य महारथात्। गदया चतुरो वाहान् राज्ञस्तस्य तदाऽवधीत्॥१२॥
verses.english: Thereupon descending from his huge car Trigarta, with bow in hand, slew the four horses of the king with his mace.

verses.sanskrit: तमभ्याशगतं राजा पदातिं कुन्तिनन्दनः। अर्धचन्द्रेण बाणेन विव्याधोरसि धर्मराट्॥१३॥
verses.english: Seeing the enemy approach so near and fighting on foot the pious king Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, pierced his breast with a crescent-shaped shaft.

verses.sanskrit: स भिन्नहृदयो वीरो वक्त्राच्छोणितमुद्वमन्। पपाताभिमुखः पार्थं छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः॥१४॥
verses.english: Thus struck on the breast that hero began to vomit blood and fell down on earth like an uprooted tree by the side of Pritha's son.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रसेनद्वितीयस्तु रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य धर्मराट्। हताश्वः सहदेवस्य प्रतिपेदे महारथम्॥१५॥
verses.english: Having his horse thus slain the pious king, with Indrasena, descended from his chariot and got upon the huge car of Sahadeva.

verses.sanskrit: नकुलं त्वभिसन्धाय क्षेमङ्करमहामुखौ। उभावुभयतस्तीक्ष्णैः शरवर्षैरवर्षताम्॥१६॥
verses.english: Then singling out Nakula, the two heroes Kshemankara and Mahamukha began to hurl at him from both sides with keen-edged arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तोमरैरभिवर्षन्तौ जीमूताविव वार्षिकौ। एकैकेन विपाठेन जघ्ने माद्रवतीसुतः॥१७॥
verses.english: With two arrows however the son of Madri succeeded in killing those two heroes who had been pouring on him a shower of arrows like clouds in rains.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिगर्तराजः सुरथस्तस्याथ रथधूर्गतः। रथमाक्षेपयामास गजेन गजयानवित्॥१८॥
verses.english: Going to the front of Nakula's chariot, Suratha, the king of Trigarta, expert in driving elephants, caused it to be dragged by the elephant of which he mounted.

verses.sanskrit: नकुलस्त्वपभीस्तस्माद्रथाच्चार्मासिपाणिमान्। उद्भ्रान्तं स्थानमास्थाय तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः॥१९॥
verses.english: Little afraid at this, Nakula jumped out of his car and securing an advantageous position, stood, shield and sword in hand immoveable as a hill.

verses.sanskrit: सुरथस्तं गजवरं वधाय नकुलस्य तु। प्रेषयामास सक्रोधमत्युच्छ्रितकरं ततः॥२०॥
verses.english: Thereupon desiring to kill Nakula at once Suratha goaded his huge and infuriated elephant with its trunk upraised (to rush towards him).

verses.sanskrit: नकुलस्तस्य नागस्य समीपपरिवर्तिनः। स विषाणं भुजं मूले खड्गेन निरकृन्तत॥२१॥
verses.english: But he with his sword cut off from his head both trunk and tusks when the elephant came near him.

verses.sanskrit: स विनद्य महानादं गजः किङ्किणिभूषणः। पतन्नवाक्शिरा भूमौ हस्त्यारोहमपोथयत्॥२२॥
verses.english: Then emitting a loud noise that elephant, clad with mail, fell headlong upon the ground crushing its riders by its fall.
verses.bhavadeepa: सविषाणं भुजं सदन्तं शुण्डादण्डम् । मूले गण्डप्रदेशे ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: स तत् कर्म महत् कृत्वा शूरो माद्रवतीसुतः। भीमसेनरथं प्राप्य शर्म लेभे महारथः॥२३॥
verses.english: Performing that great exploit the heroic and mighty car-warrior, son of the Madri, ascending Bhimasen's car, got some rest.

verses.sanskrit: भीमस्त्वापततो राज्ञः कोटिकास्यस्य सङ्गरे। सुतस्य नुदतो वाहान् क्षुरेणापाहरच्छिरः॥२४॥
verses.english: Beholding the prince Kotikasya rush to the battle, Bhima, with a horse shoe shaft, sundered the head of his charioteer.

verses.sanskrit: न बुबोध हतं सूतं स राजा बाहुशालिना। तस्याश्वा व्यद्रवन् सङ्ख्ये हतसूतास्ततस्ततः॥२५॥
verses.english: The king could not perceive that his charioteer had been slain by the mighty-armed (enemy). The horses, no longer restrained by the driver, ran about hither and thither in the battle field.

verses.sanskrit: विमुखं हतसूतं तं भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। जघान तलयुक्तेन प्रासेनाभ्येत्य पाण्डवः॥२६॥
verses.english: The Pandava Bhima, the foremost of heroes, slew, with a bearded arrow, that prince who had lost his chariot and was flying from the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: द्वादशानां तु सर्वेषां सौवीराणां धनञ्जयः। चकर्त निशितैर्भल्लैर्धनूंषि च शिरांसि च॥२७॥
verses.english: With his sharp crescent-shaped shafts Dhananjaya also cut off the heads and bows of all the twelve Sauvira heroes.
verses.bhavadeepa: तलयुक्तेन मुष्टियुक्तेन ‘तलं स्वरूपे-’ इत्युपक्रम्य ‘चपेटे च त्सरौ’ इति मोदनी । त्सरुः खड्गादिमुष्टिः ॥२६॥

verses.sanskrit: शिबीनिक्ष्वाकुमुख्यांश्च त्रिगर्तान् सैन्धवानपि। जघानातिरथः सङ्ख्ये बाणगोचरमागतान्॥२८॥
verses.english: That great warrior slew with shafts in battle, the leader of the Ikshvakus, the army of the Shibis, Trigarta and Saindhava.

verses.sanskrit: सादिताः प्रत्यदृश्यन्त बहवः सव्यसाचिना। सपताकाश्च मातङ्गाः सध्वजाश्च महारथाः॥२९॥
verses.english: Many elephants with flags and great cars with standards were to have been destroyed by Savyasachi. seen

verses.sanskrit: प्रच्छाद्य पृथिवीं तस्थुः सर्वमायोधनं प्रति। शरीराण्यशिरस्कानि विदेहानि शिरांसि च॥३०॥
verses.english: There lay covering the entire field of battle heads without trunks and trunks without heads.

verses.sanskrit: श्वगृध्रकङ्ककाकोलभासगोमायुवायसाः। अतृप्यंस्तत्र वीराणां हतानां मांसशोणितैः॥३१॥
verses.english: Dogs, heroes, ravens, crows, falcons, jackals and vultures feasted on the flesh and blood of the heroes killed in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: हतेषु तेषु वीरेषु सिन्धुराजो जयद्रथः। विमुच्य कृष्णां सन्त्रस्तः पलायनमनाऽभवत्॥३२॥
verses.english: Beholding his warriors slain, Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu became terrified and anxious to run away leaving Krishna behind.

verses.sanskrit: स तस्मिन् संकुले सैन्ये द्रौपदीमवतार्य ताम्। प्राणप्रेप्सुरुपाधावद्वनं येन नराधमः॥३३॥
verses.english: Getting Draupadi down, the wretch, in the confusion, fled away for life following the same forest path by which he had come.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदीं धर्मराजस्तु दृष्ट्वा धौम्यपुरस्कृताम्। माद्रीपुत्रेण वीरेण रथमारोपयत् तदा॥३४॥
verses.english: Beholding Draupadi with Dhaumya walking before, the pious king Yudhishthira made her taken up on the car by the heroic Sahadeva, the son of Madri.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तद्विद्रुतं सैन्यमपयाते जयद्रथे। आदिश्यादिश्य नाराचैराजघान वृकोदरः॥३५॥
verses.english: After Jayadratha had fled away Vrikodara, with Narachas, slew all those soldiers who were running away, marking (each one of them).

verses.sanskrit: सव्यसाची तु तं दृष्ट्वा पलायन्तं जयद्रथम्। वारयामास निघ्नन्तं भीमं सैन्धवसैनिकान्॥३६॥
verses.english: Beholding Jayadratha fled, Savyasachi asked Bhima to desist from killing the remnant of the Saindhava army.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच।
              यस्यापचारात् प्राप्तोऽयमस्मान् क्लेशो दुरासदः। तमस्मिन् समरोद्देशे न पश्यामि जयद्रथम्॥३७॥
verses.english: Arjuna said: I do not see Jayadratha in the battle-field through whose folly we have met with this misfortune.

verses.sanskrit: तमेवान्विष भद्रं ते किं ते योधैर्निपातितैः। अनामिषमिदं कर्म कथं वा मन्यते भवान्॥३८॥
verses.english: Seek him out; may good betide you. What is the use of killing these soldiers? Why are you bent upon this useless business?

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              इत्युक्तो भीमसेनस्तु गुडाकेशेन धीमता। युधिष्ठिरमभिप्रेक्ष्य वाग्मी वचनमब्रवीत्॥३९॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Being thus accosted by the intelligent Gudakesha, Bhimasena, skilled in speech, turning to Yudhishthira, said,

verses.sanskrit: हतप्रवीरा रिपवो भूयिष्ठं विद्रुता दिशः। गृहीत्वा द्रौपदीं राजन्निवर्ततु भवानितः॥४०॥
verses.english: "Many of the enemy's heroes have been slain; others have fled away to various directions; taking Draupadi with you, O king, return home.

verses.sanskrit: यमाभ्यां सह राजेन्द्र धौम्येन च महात्मना। प्राप्याश्रमपदं राजन् द्रौपदीं परिसान्त्वय॥४१॥
verses.english: O king of kings, O king, reaching hermitage with the twins and the high-souled Dhaumya console Draupadi.

verses.sanskrit: न हि मे मोक्ष्यते जीवन् मूढः सैन्धवको नृपः। पातालतलसंस्थोऽपि यदि शक्रोऽस्य सारथिः॥४२॥
verses.english: I shall not let along the stupid king of Sindhu even if he finds shelter in the nether world or is supported by Indra himself.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              न हन्तव्यो महाबाहो दुरात्माऽपि स सैन्धवः। दुःशलामभिसंस्मृत्य गान्धारीं च यशस्विनीम्॥४३॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said: O you of mighty arms, remembering our sister Dushala and the illustrious Gandhari, the wicked-minded Saindhava should not be slain by you.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तच्छ्रुत्वा द्रौपदी भीममुवाच व्याकुलेन्द्रिया। कुपिता ह्रीमती प्राज्ञा पती भीमार्जुनावुभौ॥४४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said: Hearing those words Draupadi was excited; that bashful, angry and intelligent (lady) said to her husbands Bhima and Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: कर्तव्यं चेत् प्रियं मह्यं वध्यः स पुरुषाधमः। सैन्धवापसदः पापो दुर्मतिः कुलपांसनः॥४५॥
verses.english: “If you wish to encompass my pleasure, that vile, wretch of a man, the wicked-minded, infamous and despicable king of the Saindhava race should be killed by you.

verses.sanskrit: भार्याभिहर्ता वैरी यो यश्च राज्यहरो रिपुः। याचमानोऽपि सङ्ग्रामे न मोक्तव्यः कथञ्चन॥४६॥
verses.english: The enemy who carries away one's wife or wrests his kingdom, should by no means be forgiven in battle even if he craves for mercy.”

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तौ तौ नरव्याघ्रौ ययतुर्यत्र सैन्धवः। राजा निववृते कृष्णामादाय सपुरोहितः॥४७॥
verses.english: Having been thus addressed those two foremost of men went where Saindhava was; taking Draupadi with him, the king alone with his priest returned.

verses.sanskrit: स प्रविश्याश्रमपदमपविद्धवृसीमठम्। मार्कण्डेयादिभिर्विप्रैरनुकीर्णं ददर्श ह॥४८॥
verses.english: Entering the hermitage he saw it covered with the seats for the ascetics, filled with their disciples and graced with the presence of Markandeya and other Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदीमनुशोचद्भिर्ब्राह्मणैस्तैः समाहितैः। समियाय महाप्राज्ञः सभार्यो भ्रातृमध्यगः॥४९॥
verses.english: While those self-controlled Brahmanas where lamenting for Draupadi, the greatly wise (king) with his wife and brothers joined them.
verses.bhavadeepa: अपविद्धा इतस्ततो विशीर्णा वृस्यो ऋषीणामासनानि मठाश्च छात्राणामालया यत्र तत् ॥४८॥

verses.sanskrit: ते स्म तं मुदिता दृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रत्यागतं नृपम्। जित्वा तान् सिन्धुसौवीरान् द्रौपदीं चाहतां पुनः॥५०॥
verses.english: Beholding the king then return, having vanquished the Sindhu and Sauvira princes and taken Draupadi, they were delighted.

verses.sanskrit: स तैः परिवृतो राजा तत्रैवोपविवेश ह। प्रविवेशाश्रमं कृष्णा यमाभ्यां सह भाविनी॥५१॥
verses.english: Encircled by them the king sat there and the good Krishna, alone with the twins, entered the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनार्जुनौ चापि श्रुत्वा क्रोशगतं रिपुम्। स्वयमश्वांस्तुदन्तौ तौ जवेनैवाभ्यधावताम्॥५२॥
verses.english: Hearing that the enemy has gone only two miles Bhima and Arjuna spurred their horses to greatest speed in pursuit of him.

verses.sanskrit: इदमत्यद्भुतं चात्र चकार पुरुषोऽर्जुनः। क्रोशमात्रगतानश्वान् सैन्धवस्य जघान् यत्॥५३॥
verses.english: The heroic Arjuna performed a wonderful fcat by killing the horses of Saindhava, which were at a distance of two miles.

verses.sanskrit: स हि दिव्यास्त्रसम्पन्नः कृच्छ्रकालेऽप्यसम्भ्रमः। अकरोद्दुष्करं कर्म शरैरस्त्रानुमन्त्रितैः॥५४॥
verses.english: Armed with celestials weapons and undaunted by difficulties he performed this difficult work with weapons inspired with Mantras.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽभ्यधावतां वीरावुभौ भीमधनञ्जयौ। हताश्वं सैन्धवं भीतमेकं व्याकुलचेतसम्॥५५॥
verses.english: Then the two heroes Bhima and Arjuna rushed towards the terror-stricken king of Sindhu whose horses had been killed and who was perplexed in mind.

verses.sanskrit: सैन्धवस्तु हतान् दृष्ट्वा तथाऽश्वान्स्वान् सुदुःखितः। अतिविक्रमकर्माणि कुर्वाणं च धनञ्जयम्॥५६॥
verses.english: Beholding his own horses slain and Dhananjaya perform such a greatly powerful exploits Saindhava was greatly sorry.

verses.sanskrit: पलायनकृतोत्साहः प्राद्रवद्येन वै वनम्। सैन्धवं त्वभिसम्प्रेक्ष्य पराक्रान्तं पलायने॥५७॥
verses.english: Determined on flying away he followed the same forest path by which he had come. Beholding Saindhava thus engaged in flying away.

verses.sanskrit: अनुयाय महाबाहुः फाल्गुनो वाक्यमब्रवीत्। अनेन वीर्येण कथं स्त्रियं प्रार्थयसे बलात्॥५८॥
verses.english: The mighty-armed Falguna, following him, said "with such prowess how could you desire to take away a female by force?

verses.sanskrit: राजपुत्र निवर्तस्व न ते युक्तं पलायनम्। कथं ह्यनुचरान् हित्वा शत्रुमध्ये पलायसे॥५९॥
verses.english: Desist, O princes it does not behoove you, leaving your followers in the midst of enemies, to take to your heels?

verses.sanskrit: इत्युच्यमानः पार्थेन सैन्धवो न न्यवर्तत। तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति तं भीमः सहसाऽभ्यद्रवद्वली। मावधीरिति पार्थस्तं दयावान् प्रत्यभाषत॥६०॥
verses.english: (Although) addressed by Partha thus Saindhava did not return. Saying "Wait, wait! the mighty Bhima all on a sudden overtook him. But the merciful Partha said, "Don't kill him."
